units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So why do people say Antwerp was once the richest city in Europe?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Let me soften that. Around 1560 it was the second-largest city in Europe north of the Alps.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the claim the sources support.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So second place.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Second place in a very big field.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the reason comes down to geography and luck.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Luck?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Around 1500, the channel to the old trading city of Bruges silted up.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Ships couldn't get in easily.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So the merchants moved?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They moved to Antwerp, where the river was deep and the harbor was open.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Foreign trading houses set up here in the late 15th century.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Like a business park for the whole continent.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Roughly. And the money came in waves.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pepper from the Portuguese. Silver from the Spanish route to the Americas.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Cloth from the north.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And what did the merchants do with all of it?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They traded it. And in 1531, Antwerp opened its stock exchange, the first building designed from scratch for the job.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A building just for trading.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Just for trading. Before that, merchants met in squares and inns.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Antwerp gave it a roof.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Which means they invented the office.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That is not quite the word. But I'll allow it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'll take it. So rich city. Beautiful buildings, I assume?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Very. In 1565 the new town hall opened on the main square.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A Renaissance building, designed by Cornelis Floris and Willem van den Broeck.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Hold on to that one. You'll stand in front of it tomorrow.
